subject: SOW exhibit recast: implementation milestones + billing cadence clarification
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@medsys.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Roberto Diaz <rdiaz@medsys.com>
Date: 2028-07-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recasting Exhibit D — request for clarity on milestones and billing

Marcus — thanks for the call this morning. As we discussed, MedSys is proceeding with the pilot but we need stronger clarity in Exhibit D: a) firm implementation milestones with acceptance criteria, and b) billing cadence when we cross the 500 GPU-hour threshold (and the mechanism for prorated credits during mid-month top-ups).

Attached is a version of Exhibit D with inline comments (redlines from our side). Key asks:
- Move the acceptance window to 10 business days from completion and add a bulletized checklist for acceptance tests.
- Define a clear prorate formula for any mid-billing-cycle capacity increases.
- Add a rollback clause if latency regressions > 30% post-rollout for two consecutive weeks.

Can your legal and procurement team review and confirm whether these are acceptable or propose alternate language? We’re trying to lock the orderform this week so implementation can start 7/18.

Best,
Tara
Director, CloudOps
MedSys Health

Attachments: MedSys_SOW_ExhibitD_redline_v3.docx (docx, 45KB)

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@medsys.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-08T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recasting Exhibit D — request for clarity on milestones and billing

Hi Tara — appreciate the clear redlines and the quick turnaround. Looping in Naomi (Contracts) and Laura (Implementation PM) to evaluate the proposed acceptance checklist and prorate formula. Our initial thoughts:

- Implementation schedule: we can commit to the 7/18 start but need to lock the milestone acceptance tests to avoid ambiguous sign-offs. Laura will draft a 6-item acceptance checklist aligned to your comments.
- Proration: we typically prorate at the daily token/GPU-hour level for mid-cycle increases; happy to map this to your language, and include an example calculation in Exhibit D.
- Latency rollback: rollback clauses can be risky if tied to a numeric threshold without guardrails. Naomi, can Legal propose fallback language that allows remediation windows and performance engineering support before automatic rollback?

Action items:
1) Laura to draft acceptance checklist and timing (ETA EOD 7/08).
2) Naomi to propose redline language for rollback and proration (ETA 7/09).
3) Marcus to circulate combined Exhibit D and pricing reconciliation once legal and PM align.

Thanks — we’ll aim to have a clean exhibit for DocuSign by end of next week.

—Marcus
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: implementation-matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-09T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Recasting Exhibit D — request for clarity on milestones and billing

Marcus / Laura — quick pass on legal redlines below (draft language included inline in the attached doc):

1) Acceptance window: we can accept a 10 business day review window but need to explicitly state the acceptance criteria and a default acceptance mechanic (i.e., if MedSys does not provide written rejection within 10 business days, the milestone is deemed accepted). This avoids indefinite hold-ups.

2) Proration: propose replacing "prorate at daily GPU-hour" with a clear formula: (additional GPU-hours purchased / remaining days in billing cycle) * daily rate. Example row added to Exhibit D. Keep our currency of record and tax treatment consistent with Order Form.

3) Latency rollback: replace hard numeric rollback with staged remediation: (a) notify Redwood with performance metrics, (b) 5 business day remediation window with joint triage, (c) if unresolved after remediation window, customer may request temporary capacity reallocation or termination of affected tranche only. This protects both parties.

I attach MedSys_SOW_ExhibitD_redline_v3.docx with tracked changes. If acceptable, we sign and update the order form with the revised fee table (see pricing-reconciliation_0708.xlsx).

Naomi
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MedSys_SOW_ExhibitD_redline_v3.docx (docx, 72KB); pricing-reconciliation_0708.xlsx (xlsx, 9KB)

From: Tara Singh <tara@medsys.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, Roberto Diaz <rdiaz@medsys.com>
Date: 2028-07-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recasting Exhibit D — request for clarity on milestones and billing

Thanks Naomi — that staged remediation approach is reasonable. A couple of requests from our side:

- Can we make the default-acceptance mechanic optional instead of automatic? MedSys wants the ability to withhold acceptance if a nonconformity is suspected and requires follow-up. We can agree to "deemed accepted" but only for administrative checkpoints (documentation/completion), not for functional or performance-related acceptance.
- For proration examples, please show a pricing row for a mid-month upgrade that crosses our 500 GPU-hour internal threshold so our billing team can validate.

If you can add language for the conditional deemed-acceptance carve-out and the additional example, we should be able to sign soon. Also happy to do a 15-min call this afternoon to walk the exhibit with your PM.

Best,
Tara

Attachment: none

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@medsys.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-09T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recasting Exhibit D — request for clarity on milestones and billing

Hi Tara — thanks. I updated the implementation checklist and added the mid-cycle proration example that shows crossing 500 GPU-hours (see pricing-reconciliation_0708.xlsx). Per Naomi and Marcus, we've split acceptance into two buckets: "Administrative Acceptance" (10 business days deemed accepted if no administrative rejection) and "Functional Acceptance" (requires explicit written sign-off or completion of remediation). That should address your carve-out.

If you're free at 4:30pm PT I can jump on a 15-min screen share to walk the two examples and confirm the DocuSign timeline. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a proposed DocuSign envelope link once legal confirms final redlines.

Action items closed by this email: Laura -> updated checklist + example; Naomi -> legal language in docx; Marcus -> consolidate and send final Order Form.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Implementation Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-reconciliation_0708.xlsx (xlsx, 9KB)
